newsitem.title: USA: Dow extends losses, NYSE re-imposes curbs.
newsitem.headline: Dow extends losses, NYSE re-imposes curbs.

text.p: U.S. blue chips extended their losses, in afternoon activity on Monday, sending the Dow industrials down more than 60 points.
The Dow fell 62 points to 7834. The New York Stock Exchange said it re-imposed index-arbitrage trading curbs at 1444 EDT/1844 GMT, after the Dow's decline briefly brushed past the 50-point mark.
Earlier, the NYSE had imposed curbs when the Dow advanced 50 points during a morning rally.
Analysts continued to view the selling as routine profit-taking, noting that market volume levels appeared to be dwindling from the heavy activity registered during the most recent ascent.

"The market's entitled to a bit of a rest here," said Al Goldman, market analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons. "Markets don't top out after very good rallies; they top out after poor rallies, and this has been a very good rally."
